finding.claim: SQL injection in /search. The q query parameter is interpolated straight into the SQL string with an f-string, so an unauthenticated attacker can alter the query. They can UNION-select other tables or columns (for example the price column, or any table in shop.db) and read them back in the JSON response. The sqlite3 execute() call allows only one statement, so stacked queries are not possible, but data exfiltration is.
finding.sink: db.execute(f"SELECT id, name FROM products WHERE name LIKE '%{term}%'") at app.py:12

trace.note: term = request.args.get('q', '') takes the raw user input with no validation
term is formatted into the SQL text with an f-string
Query results are returned to the caller via jsonify, which makes UNION-based exfiltration directly visible

finding.guards_checked: No parameterization, escaping, allow-list or length limit on term. No authentication or authorization decorator on the route. No WAF or middleware in app.py. The other two routes use ? placeholders (app.py:18, app.py:25), so they are not injectable.

verdict.reason: app.py:11 reads q raw and app.py:12 f-string-interpolates it into the SQL with no auth, escaping or parameterization, and app.py:13 returns the rows via jsonify, so UNION exfiltration works (the other routes at app.py:18 and app.py:25 do use ? placeholders).

verdict_facts.reason: app.py:11 reads q raw and app.py:12 f-string-interpolates it into the SQL with no parameterization, auth decorator, or allowlist, and app.py:13 returns the rows via jsonify, so UNION-based exfiltration works (the other routes at app.py:18 and app.py:25 use placeholders, as the finding says).
